# Where the index lands beside a bibliography

Quarto appends a document's reference block after this filter has already
placed the index, so a document that leaves the bibliography where Quarto
puts it gets the index first and the references after. An empty `#refs` div
is what settles the order the other way: Quarto fills that div in place, and
a placement marker written below it puts the index after the references.

This document and its twin differ in the `#refs` div block and nothing else,
so the pair shows that the div is what moves the index rather than anything
else about the document. The `References` heading this document writes is its
own: in HTML, Quarto supplies a heading and an appendix wrapper only when it
appends the reference block itself.

An [otter]{.index} swims [@doe2020], and a [widget]{.index} does not
[@roe2018].

# Afterword {#qi-afterword}

Prose after the marker, so the marker's own work is visible: the index lands
here, above this section, rather than at the end of the document. Delete the
marker and the index falls below this section instead, which is the half of
the recipe the `#refs` div alone cannot show.
